nutshell: Perspective distortion (PD) - the shape/angle changes from camera position, focal length, and viewpoint - degrades computer vision models, but there's no real-world PD training data and estimating camera parameters to correct it is hard. MPD instead synthesizes realistic-looking PD by applying a fine-grained parametrized family of Mobius transforms (a conformal, non-linear complex-plane mapping) directly to images, with no camera-parameter estimation needed, and shows this synthetic distortion improves model robustness when used as a data augmentation across a new benchmark and four real-world PD-affected applications (crowd counting, fisheye recognition, person re-identification, object detection). Not primarily a person-ReID paper - a general representation-robustness method that happens to include ReID as one of four downstream applications, which is presumably why it surfaced in this corpus's broader search terms.
contributions: MPD: a specific family of Mobius transforms (complex-plane conformal maps, controlled via a complex parameter c) applied directly to image pixel coordinates to synthesize realistic perspective distortion (left/right/top/bottom views at controllable intensity) without estimating any camera intrinsic/extrinsic parameters or needing real distorted images.

ImageNet-PD: a new benchmark derived from the ImageNet validation set with 8 distortion subsets (4 orientations x with/without background padding), showing that standard architectures from AlexNet to ViT-B-16 all suffer large Top-1/Top-5 accuracy drops under this synthetic distortion.

MPD used as a training-time augmentation in both supervised (from-scratch) and self-supervised (SimCLR, DINO) settings, improving average Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-PD by roughly 9-10 points over an unaugmented ResNet50 while leaving original ImageNet validation accuracy essentially unchanged, and also improving on two existing partial-PD benchmarks, ImageNet-E and ImageNet-X.

Demonstrated transfer of MPD-pretrained/fine-tuned representations to four real-world PD-affected tasks: a new crowd-counting method (MPD-AutoCrowd) reporting improved MAE on ShanghaiTech and UCF-CC50; fisheye image multi-label classification on VOC-360; person re-identification on DeepSportradar via CLIP-ReIdent; and object detection on COCO via FasterRCNN/FCOS.
deficiencies: On ShanghaiTech Part B, the paper's own Table 2 shows both MPD variants regressing versus their own base method: P2P-Net (the un-augmented backbone MPD-CC and MPD-AutoCrowd are built on, same VGG16 architecture) achieves MAE 6.25, while MPD-CC gets 6.73 and MPD-AutoCrowd gets 6.61 - i.e., adding the proposed augmentation makes this specific metric on this specific dataset worse than the unaugmented baseline it's built on, which isn't acknowledged in the text's framing that 'MPD-CC and MPD-AutoCrowd outperform on multiple benchmarks.'

The person-ReID result (Table 4) is reported as 'MPD-incorporated Clip-ReIdent models improve performance with both backbone architectures,' but the improvement is backbone-dependent in magnitude the text doesn't distinguish: for ViT-L-14 the gain is negligible (96.90->97.02 mAP w/o re-ranking, +0.12; 98.20->98.30 with re-ranking, +0.10), while for ResNet50x16 it's substantial (88.50->91.95, +3.45; 94.90->97.50, +2.60) - presenting both as comparable 'improvements' obscures that one is within likely noise and the other is a real effect.

Each downstream application (crowd counting, person ReID, object detection, and the core ImageNet experiments) uses a different hand-set probability P and different ranges for the real/imaginary components of parameter c (e.g. P=0.1 with c in [0.2,0.6] for crowd counting/ReID vs. P=0.5 for object detection vs. c in [0.2,0.3] for the main ImageNet results), with no reported principled selection procedure or cross-task sensitivity analysis - a concern for a method whose central claim is general-purpose, task-agnostic distortion robustness.

The crowd-counting comparison table (Table 2) pools results from methods spanning 2019-2023 with different backbones and training recipes (CAN, Bayesian+, S-DCNet, ADSCNet, P2P-Net, etc.) without a backbone-controlled ablation isolating the Mobius augmentation's own contribution from the choice of base method (P2P-Net) itself - the one same-backbone comparison available (P2P-Net vs. +MPD) is the SHTech-B regression noted above, not a clean win.
notable: The core idea - using a closed-form conformal complex-analysis transform (Mobius transform) rather than a learned or GAN-based distortion model - is a notably cheap, dependency-free way to synthesize a specific, controllable class of image distortion; the four real components of the transform (a, b, c, d) map cleanly to interpretable operations (c controls perspective-like distortion orientation/intensity, a/d control scaling and rotation, b controls translation), which could be reused as a lightweight augmentation primitive well outside the distortion-robustness use case tested here.
